clue.text: Dry half of crockery up in silence

indicators.note: in tells us the reversed half-word sits inside the word for silence

parts.note: SH is the call for silence, hush

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, so backwards
half of takes the first four of the eight letters of crockery

explanation.surface: Someone drying the crockery and putting it away without a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' as a verb means parch with heat; 'up' works because this is a down clue, read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch something is to dry it out with intense heat, a strong synonym for parch.

clue.text: Ignore extremes of lunacy without showing one's feelings

parts.note: to blank someone is to ignore them pointedly

indicators.note: extremes of picks the first and last letters of the word lunacy

explanation.surface: Advice to shrug off madness while keeping a poker face.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking at someone blankly means with an expressionless face that reveals no emotion.

clue.text: Colleague having a small tossed lettuce. I scoffed

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: tossed here means flipped over, so the lettuce word is read backwards

parts.note: cos is a crisp variety of lettuce
to scoff food is to eat it greedily, so scoffed gives ate

explanation.surface: A coworker with a little salad that the speaker wolfed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossed' looks like a salad term for an anagram but simply flips COS to SOC.
explanation.definitionFit: An associate is a partner or fellow worker, a straightforward synonym for a colleague.

clue.text: Daughter with query about mother's stuff

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

indicators.note: about tells us the word for query goes around the mother word

parts.note: to query is to ask
MA is an informal word for mother; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A daughter asking about her mother's belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' looks like belongings but means fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a rich woven fabric, and stuff is an old word for woven material or cloth.

clue.text: Tears shed before Tevez finally makes substitute

indicators.note: shed here suggests something cast off and knocked out of shape, so the letters of tears are rearranged
finally takes the last letter of the footballer's name Tevez

explanation.surface: Tears from footballer Carlos Tevez as he is brought off the bench as a replacement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz means an inferior replacement or imitation of the real thing.

clue.text: He's getting married in record time — they won't last

indicators.note: in places the pair of pieces inside the record and time words

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
an era is a period of time
taken as he; the 's is a link meaning is
M is the abbreviation for married in genealogy and forms

explanation.surface: A man getting wed in record time, with a cynic noting such marriages fail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record time' reads as a single phrase meaning very fast, but the two words supply separate pieces that sandwich the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are things that are short-lived or transitory, such as collectable printed matter meant for a day.

clue.text: Reel from retrospective cuts putting the squeeze on old

indicators.note: the reversed cuts word hugs the letter for old, enclosing it
retrospective means looking back, so the word for cuts is read backwards

parts.note: to lop is to cut off branches, so cuts gives lops

explanation.surface: A film reel taken from a retrospective season, with some edits squeezing older footage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospective' turns LOPS into SPOL, which wraps O.
explanation.definitionFit: A spool is a cylinder on which thread or film is wound, the same thing as a reel.

clue.text: Conflict about essentially horrible instrument

indicators.note: about tells us the conflict word goes round the central letters

parts.note: a tangle is a dispute or fight, as in to tangle with someone

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the central two letters of horrible

explanation.surface: A row breaking out over an awful musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle is a percussion instrument, a steel bar bent into three sides and struck.

clue.text: Cheryl's regulation salad

parts.note: Cheryl Cole is a British pop singer, formerly of Girls Aloud; her possessive gives Cole's
a law is a rule or regulation

explanation.surface: A rule laid down by the singer Cheryl.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheryl Cole is a British pop star and TV talent-show judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleslaw is a salad of shredded raw cabbage and carrot in mayonnaise.

clue.text: Swimming coach admitting start of training before international is disorganised

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the shuffled coach letters take in the other pieces
swimming suggests letters floating about and rearranged
before places the training letter ahead of the international letter
start of takes the first letter of training

explanation.surface: A swimming coach who lets training start just before an international meet is badly organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimming' shuffles COACH to CHAOC, and 'admitting' takes TI inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaotic means in complete disorder, which is what disorganised describes.

clue.text: One of four players with some flair in golf

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A member of a foursome with some talent on the golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: The four players are not golfers but the Beatles.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringo Starr was the drummer of the Beatles, a band of four musicians.

clue.text: Making shaky progress with fake jewellery

parts.note: a sham is a fake or imitation
bling is slang for flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: Someone tottering along weighed down with costume jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Shambling means walking in an awkward, unsteady, shuffling way.

clue.text: Knock success

definitions.meaning: a success, as in a chart ... or smash

explanation.definitionFit: Hit means both a blow struck and a popular success such as a hit record.

clue.text: He's left to invest independent capital

parts.note: taken as he; the 's is a link meaning has
to sink money into something is to invest it

explanation.surface: A man has funds left over to put into an independent venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invest' looks like a container signal but gives SINK.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital city of Finland.

clue.text: Row with the French causing anger

parts.note: a rank is a row, as in a line of soldiers or a taxi rank
le is the masculine form of the in French

explanation.surface: A French row that leaves people furious.
explanation.definitionFit: To rankle is to cause lasting irritation or resentment, a verb sense matching to anger.

clue.text: I've connected a lead wrongly? That's hearsay

indicators.note: wrongly suggests the letters have been put together incorrectly and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone unsure whether they wired a lead correctly, told it is only rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence based on stories and personal accounts rather than facts amounts to hearsay.

clue.text: See 15
After end of concert run out of time to get something to drink

indicators.note: after places the other piece behind the concert letter
end of takes the last letter of concert
out of means the run letter is removed from the time word

parts.note: an era is a period of time
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: After a concert ends there is no time left to grab a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run out of time' looks like a phrase but means R taken out of ERA, leaving EA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a hot beverage, a drink brewed from leaves.

clue.text: Forever losing her head, Hetty cuddles short straight man

indicators.note: cuddles means hugs, so the shortened name goes around the other piece
losing her head drops the first letter of the name Hetty
short means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: Ernie Wise was the straight man of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: Hetty, in a daze, hugging a short comedian's sidekick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing her head' leaves ETTY, and 'short' cuts ERNIE to ERNI.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternity means endless time, as in lasting forever.

clue.text: Musical intro before a new piece

indicators.note: intro takes the opening letter of musical

explanation.surface: An overture before a fresh musical number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' looks like a piece of music but is a chess or draughts piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A man is a piece in board games such as chess or draughts.

clue.text: Wader at cove is floundering

indicators.note: floundering means struggling clumsily, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A wading bird struggling in a small bay.
explanation.definitionFit: An avocet is a black-and-white wading bird with an upturned bill.

clue.text: Drug found in sink

definitions.meaning: to sink a ball in snooker or billiards

explanation.definitionFit: Pot is slang for cannabis and also means to send a ball into a pocket.

clue.text: Prime time gets you down

parts.note: plum means choice or prime, as in a plum job
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Feeling depressed during the best years of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like gloom but means soft feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumage is a bird's feathers, and down is its fine soft feathering.

clue.text: In relating to vision artist is prophetic

indicators.note: in places the artist letters inside the vision word

parts.note: ocular means relating to the eyes or sight
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: An artist's vision described as foretelling the future.
explanation.definitionFit: Oracular means like an oracle, uttering prophecies or cryptic predictions.

clue.text: Discount rule taking the edge off discussion

indicators.note: the edge is the first letter, so the discussion word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a debate is a formal discussion

explanation.surface: A discount policy that softens a tense negotiation.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebate is a partial refund or reduction in price, a discount.

clue.text: Indignation after that woman returns book again

indicators.note: after places the indignation word behind the other piece
returns means the word for that woman comes back reversed

parts.note: her refers to a woman already mentioned
ire is anger or indignation

explanation.surface: An angry woman taking a library book back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns book' looks like a library visit, but 'book again' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehire someone is to engage them again, much as you book a performer again.

clue.text: Outline faintly in umber a tad carelessly

indicators.note: carelessly suggests the letters have been dashed off untidily and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter sketching roughly in brown pigment.
explanation.walkthrough: Umber is a brown earth pigment.
explanation.definitionFit: To adumbrate is to sketch or indicate in outline, giving a faint impression.

clue.text: End up with expression of pain in response to spiteful remark

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: an aim is an end or goal
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: Someone finishing with a yelp after being hurt by a cutting remark.
explanation.walkthrough: A spiteful remark is catty, so the answer is a cat's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying a cat's cry is the jokey retort to a catty, spiteful comment.

clue.text: Personal magnetism low around outskirts of Plymouth

indicators.note: around here means turned round, so the word for low is read backwards

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: outskirts of picks the first and last letters of Plymouth

explanation.surface: Feeling flat on the edge of a Devon city.
explanation.walkthrough: Plymouth is a port city in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is energy, vitality or sex appeal, a vigorous kind of charisma.

clue.text: Virginia wearing trendy top to no effect

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the state letters sit inside the clothing pieces

parts.note: in means fashionable
a lid is a top or cover
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Virginia in a fashionable top that fails to impress.
explanation.definitionFit: Something invalid is void, having no legal force or effect.

clue.text: Boa's lack of length is more unusual

indicators.note: lack of means the length letter is missing from the snake word

parts.note: a boa constrictor is a strangler, killing prey by squeezing; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: A snake that is shorter than expected is all the odder.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranger is the comparative of strange, meaning odder or more unusual.

clue.text: Backing small wager without room to manoeuvre

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the wager word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to lay a bet is to wager

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for small is reversed

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: Supporting a small bet that leaves no space for manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking; 'Backing' turns WEE into EEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is freedom of action or margin for error, scope to move.
